0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard ( Part XI ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 17 February 1983, after the draft finalized by the Environmental Testing Procedures Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. 0.2 The differences in environmental testing procedures for component in the context of type and equipment type items are fast disappearing It is, therefore, felt necessary to have unitechnological developments. form testing procedures wherever possible. This series of standards on environmental testing procedures ( IS : 9000 ) has been prepared with this objective. This is also in line with the principle adopted by IEC/TC 50 in developing unified series of standards on err `Environmental testing' vironmental testing procedures by the International Electrotechnical Commission. 0.2.1 It is proposed IS : 589-1961* and IS electronic components mentioned therein are to withdraw the existing Indian standards, namely, : 2106t series dealing with environmental tests for and equipment respectively, as soon as the tests covered in the new series ( IS : 9000 ). ) deals with the determination of the corrosive electronic and electrical items. assistance Salt mist. has been derived International from

1. SCOPE -1.1 This
standard ( Part XI ) gives details of test procedures for the application of salt mist test on electronic and electrical items as a part of basic environmental testing procedures.
NOTE This test is not an all-purpose corrosion test.

4.8 The conditions maintained at all parts of the working space of the chamber shall be such that a clean fog-collecting receptacle placed at any point will collect from 0.5 to 3 ml of solution per hour for each 80 square centimetres of horizontal collecting area ( 10 cm diameter ) based on an The receptacle shall be placed in such a average test of at least 16 h. manner that it is not shielded by test items and no drops of solution from test items and other sources are collected in it. 4.9 The compressed air entering the atomizer shall be essentially free from all impurities, such as oil and dirt. For this purpose, an air filter fabricated from anon-corrosive material shall be provided in the air A rolled glags wool cloth and a glass diaphragm shall be supply line. Means shall be provided to humidify and suitably placed in the filter. warm the compressed air as required to meet the operating conditions. To ensure against clogging the atomizers by salt deposition, the air should have a relative humidity of at least 85 percent at the point of A satisfactory method is to pass the air in very release from the nozzle. fine bubbles through a tower containing heated water which should be automatically maintained at a constant level. The temperature of the water should be at least 35�C. The permissible water temperature increases with increasing volume of air and with decreasing insulation However, the temof the chamber and the chamber's surroundings. perature should not exceed a value above which an excess of moisture is introduced into the chamber ( for example, 43�C at an air pressure of 85 kPa or a value which makes it impossible to meet the requirements for operating temperature ). 4.10 A suitable damp heat chamber shall be used for conditioning the items immediately after the exposure to the salt laden atmosphere as required in Procedures 2 and 3. The damp heat chamber shall be capable of maintaining its working space at a temperature of 35 + 3�C and relative humidity of 90 to 95 percent during the entire period of storage of the item under test. This chamber shall also satisfy the requirements specified for the chamber in IS : 9002 ( Part III )-1979". 5. PRECONDITIONING

INITIAL MEASUREMENTS and mechanically

6.1 The items shall be visually inspected and electrically checked, as required by the relevant specification. 7. CONDITIONING 7.1 General

7.9 : The item under test shall be subject to this test in its `unpacked' and `switched-off' condition. Three test procedures are specified for this Test Procedure 1 is applicable to component type items. Test test. Procedures 2 and 3 are applicable to equipment type items. Where an item is likely to be exposed to severe salt contamination conditions, Test Procedure 2 may be preferred and in less exacting conditions where a salt laden atmosphere will occasionally exist. Test Procedure 3 may be The rele\ ant specification shall specify any of the three test preferrec!. procedures, as necessary. 7.2 Preparation of Salt Solution

7.2.1 For Procedure 1, the salt used shall be sodium chloride containing on dry basis not more than 0.1 p.ercent sodium iodide and not more The salt solution used sha!l contain than 0.5 percent of total impurities. either 5 percent or 20 percent sodium chloric!e. The 5 percent solution unless the relevant specification specifies otherwise. shall be referred, The distilled water or demineralized water used for making the salt so!ution shall not contain more than 200 parts per million of total solids. The composition and characteristics of the salt coiution shall be as stated in Table 1. 7.2.2 For Procedures 2 and 3, the salts given in 2 shall be dissolved in distilled/demineralised water for the preparation of the salt solution. The proportions of the ingredients in the solution are to be within 10 percent of those given in Table 2. 7

Examination

7.6.1 For Procedure 1, at the end of the conditioning period speci.fied in 7.3.2, the items shall be removed from the chamber and examined for corrosion and deterioration of metal parts, finishes, materials, etc. To aid in examination, if necessary, the items may be given a gentle wash in running water not warmer than 38�C with light brushing using a soft hair brush or plastic bristle brush to r'cmove the salt deposits. The surplus water shall be removed by shaking.
7.6.2 For Procedures 2 and 3, at the end of the conditioning period specified in 7.4.5 and 7.5.5, the items, unless otherwise specified by the relevant specification, shall be washed in running tap water for five minutes, rinsed in distilled water or demineralized water and then shaken by hand or subjected to an airblast to remove droplets of lvater, then dried for one hour at 55 f 2�C and allowed to cool under recovery The relevant conditions for not less than 1 hour nor more than 2 hours. specification shall specify, if required, other methods to be used for washing and drying. The items shall be stored under recovery conditions for not less than one hour and not more than 2 hours. The temperature of the water used for washing shall not exceed 35�C. 8. RECOVERY

8.1 The items shall then be subjected

to recovery under standard atmospheric conditions for testing for a period of 2 to 4 hours, unless otherwise specified in the relevant specification.
